rubric.why: Identifies the heavy particles found in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Names protons and neutrons as the heavy particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both protons and neutrons.

rubric.why: Connects the presence of these particles in the nucleus to the concentration of the atom’s mass there.
rubric.description: States that almost all the atom’s mass is concentrated in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the atom’s mass to the nucleus.

modelAnswer: It was also discovered that almost all the mass of an atom is concentrated in the nucleus because both the heavy particles i.e. protons and neutrons are found to be present here.

rubric.why: States that elements differ in their properties.
rubric.description: Identifies a difference in the properties of elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the properties of elements differ.

rubric.why: Gives the difference in the properties of their constituent atoms as the cause.
rubric.description: Attributes the difference to the properties of constituent atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the difference in elements’ properties to their constituent atoms.

modelAnswer: The difference in the properties of elements is due to the difference in the properties of their constituent atoms.

rubric.why: Uses the relation between neutron number, mass number and atomic number.
rubric.description: States the formula for calculating the number of neutrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for N = A − Z.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given numbers or states the correct neutron count.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct result, 127 neutrons.

rubric.why: Identifies that the second shell is farther from the nucleus than the first shell.
rubric.description: States the relative distance of the second shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that the second shell is at a greater distance than the first.

rubric.why: Connects the electron’s greater distance in the second shell with its greater energy.
rubric.description: States that an electron in the second shell has greater energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the electron in the second shell possesses more energy.

modelAnswer: The second shell will also be at a definite distance from the nucleus which will, of course, be greater than the first shell and electron present in it will also possess greater value of energy.

rubric.why: Gives the classical model of electrons moving in specific paths around the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that an electron revolves around the nucleus in a specific path, or orbit/shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the classical concept of electrons revolving in specific paths.

rubric.why: Describes the modern view and the uncertainty in locating an electron.
rubric.description: States that electrons are viewed as charged clouds whose locations cannot be predicted with certainty.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the modern cloud model and uncertain electron location.

modelAnswer: According to this model the electron can revolve around the nucleus of the atom in specific paths called orbits or shells. According to modern approach, electrons are like charged clouds whose location around the nucleus cannot be predicted with one hundred percent certainty.

rubric.why: Identifies the particles held together in the nucleus.
rubric.description: Names protons and neutrons as the particles in the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

rubric.why: Names the force that holds the particles together.
rubric.description: States that a strong nuclear force holds them together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the strong nuclear force.

modelAnswer: In the nucleus these two particles are held together by a strong nuclear force.
